or on the figure a statement bound, and the floor is applied last: a claim's live due is the

request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The order of the due steps changes: the late charge is now worked out on the rate figure alone,
or on the figure a statement bound, and the floor is applied last: a claim's live due is the
greater of the floor in force on its date and its figure plus its late charge. A statement now
binds the rate figure, not the floored one. Settled figures stay frozen; a correction is unchanged
(no floor, no charge).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The new due order is in place, and all 4 acceptance tests pass with `bin/e2e`.

A claim's live due is now the greater of the floor in force on its date and its rate figure plus its late charge. The late charge is worked out on the rate figure alone, or on the figure a statement bound. Settled dues stay frozen, and a correction still gets no floor and no charge.

The due is calculated in two places, so I changed both the same way:
- **Server:** in `Claim.java`, the figure is now the plain rate figure (or the bound or settled one), and the floor is applied last when the due is worked out. Because taking a statement saves this figure, a statement now binds the rate figure rather than the floored one. I updated the comment in `TakeStatement.java` to match.
- **Front end:** `features/claims/claims.ts` works out the dues it displays itself, so `claimFigureCents` and `claimDueCents` got the same change. The first test run failed until I made it.

Statements taken before this change still hold the floored figure they saved, and I didn't rewrite them. With the new order this mostly comes out the same, because the floor is applied again at the end. The exception is an overdue claim whose floor was higher than its rate figure: its late charge will now be worked out on the floor rather than on the rate figure.

I made no database migration or audit format changes.
